bridgeRouteRisk.summary: JPYC v1 has one native owner-only issuance route on Ethereum. Polygon PoS and Gnosis OmniBridge are lock/mint representations: their destination bridge mint and burn paths, escrow or mediator accounting, message and peer configuration, proxy upgrades, bridge administrators, and validator or checkpoint machinery are assessed here rather than in Mint Authority.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex mint/bridge boundary migration; verified JPYC v1 finding

routes.reviewNote: At Ethereum block 25770969, the official JPYC v1 source and live contract state identify this direct ERC-20 as the only native issuance deployment: owner-only mint(address,uint256) remains technically live, the owner EOA is 0x94c2d94a786e1aaa07e95d084e88cd3a0680d152, and EIP-1967 implementation and admin slots are zero. Polygon and Gnosis are mapped bridge representations reviewed separately below.

At Ethereum block 25770969, RootChainManagerProxy 0xa0c68c638235ee32657e8f720a23cec1bfc77c77 resolved to implementation 0xf0235dca8fb0d3999685724dcbb9dd00c5d62dfa, rootToChildToken(JPYC) mapped to this Polygon token, tokenToType(JPYC) was keccak256(ERC20), typeToPredicate(ERC20) was ERC20PredicateProxy 0x40ec5b33f54e0e8a33a975908c5ba1c14e5bbbdf, and childChainManagerAddress() was 0xa6fa4fb5f76172d178d61b04b0ecd319c5d1c0aa. At Polygon block 92145902, the token resolved to UChildERC20 implementation 0x4350806aa2508a44aab4cb87a0eece362d882f11; its sole DEPOSITOR_ROLE member was ChildChainManagerProxy and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE had no members. The route is supply-conserving when operated correctly: the root token is locked in the ERC20 predicate, state-sync calls destination deposit() to mint, withdrawals burn child tokens, and checkpoint proof unlocks the root balance. Root mapping and proxy governance, ChildChainManager and state-sync, token-proxy upgrade authority, and checkpoint machinery remain bridge failure domains.

At Gnosis block 47762624, the JPYC token resolved to PermittableToken implementation 0xf8d1677c8a0c961938bf2f9adc3f3cfda759a9d9; its EIP-1967 admin slot was zero, and verified TokenProxy storage identified Home OmniBridge 0xf6a78083ca3e2a662d6dd1703c939c8ace2e268d as both owner and bridgeContract. Home bridgedTokenAddress(Ethereum JPYC) and Foreign foreignTokenAddress(Gnosis JPYC) mapped these deployments, and isTokenRegistered was true. The bridge token's owner-only mint is mediator-controlled and finishMinting() reverts in this image, so token-level minting is uncapped while route-level issuance depends on AMB messages, a four-of-seven validator quorum, mediator accounting, and execution limits. The reviewed Home mediator daily limit was 10^18 CGO and max-per-transaction was 10^9 CGO; the Foreign mediator, mediator owners, AMB proxies, and validator management remain bridge controls.

controls.label: JPYC Polygon ChildChainManager DEPOSITOR_ROLE
controls.capDescription: The UChildERC20 destination mint path has no independently verified token cap; route-level supply conservation depends on the Polygon PoS lock, state-sync, burn, and checkpoint-unlock sequence.

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: RootChainManager state-sync calls the Polygon ChildChainManagerProxy, whose sole DEPOSITOR_ROLE member was the manager proxy; STATE_SYNCER_ROLE was held by the Polygon state-sync system address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001001.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: Ethereum JPYC is locked in the ERC20 predicate before child deposit() minting; withdrawals burn child tokens and unlock the root predicate balance after checkpoint proof.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Polygon block 92145902, the destination UChildERC20 implementation was 0x4350806aa2508a44aab4cb87a0eece362d882f11, DEPOSITOR_ROLE had only ChildChainManagerProxy, and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE had zero members.

controls.evidence: At Polygon block 92145902, the JPYC UChildERC20 implementation exposed deposit() minting gated by DEPOSITOR_ROLE; its sole member was ChildChainManagerProxy 0xa6fa4fb5f76172d178d61b04b0ecd319c5d1c0aa and DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE had no members. This is the destination bridge mint path, not native JPYC issuance.

controls.label: JPYC Polygon UChildERC20 token proxy owner multisig
controls.capDescription: The legacy MultiSigWalletWithDailyLimit token-proxy owner can replace the UChildERC20 implementation and thereby alter destination mint, burn, and bridge-admin behavior; required() was 1 and no daily limit was configured.
controls.evidence: At Polygon block 92145902, the UChildERC20 token proxy owner was legacy MultiSigWalletWithDailyLimit 0x355b8e02e7f5301e6fac9b7cac1d6d9c86c0343f. required() returned 1, its sole owner was 0x3a635c48836e7c0b9aeb378640b0bfd516985cf5, and no daily limit was configured. This proxy-admin capability remains bridge risk because an implementation replacement can change destination mint and burn behavior.

ERC20PredicateProxy 0x40ec5b33f54e0e8a33a975908c5ba1c14e5bbbdf had the same proxy owner, so the timelock controls the Polygon lock/withdrawal bridge machinery.

controls.label: Polygon PoS checkpoint and validator proof machinery

routeChecks.attestorQuorum: Polygon PoS withdrawals require checkpoint proof before the ERC20 predicate unlocks Ethereum JPYC; this protocol-level review preserves the validator/checkpoint failure domain without assigning an unverified coin-specific validator controller.

controls.evidence: The Polygon route is supply-conserving only when checkpoint proof and the Polygon PoS validator machinery correctly authorize withdrawals and predicate unlocks. That protocol-level validator failure domain is retained as a structured Bridge Risk control; no separate coin-specific validator contract or controller was attributed in the verified JPYC route evidence.
